title: Completeness of bounded finite-free retract complexes without residue hypotheses
statement: For any scheme T, prime ell and finite extension E of Q_ell, a bounded cochain complex of completed integral coefficient sheaves whose terms split off finite free sheaves is derived complete. The scheme and coefficient universes are independent. No quasi-compactness or invertibility hypothesis on ell is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 6.5.5, finite-free retracts and bounded devissage; Stacks Tags 099I and 0941

proof.text: Choose a flat-term K-flat representative and the principal coefficient datum. The intrinsic Roos/Koszul equivalence identifies completeness with vanishing of the principal-localization internal-Hom test for every locally divisible section on each slice. An auxiliary prime distinct from ell always exists.

For a fixed slice and section, exact restriction followed by internal Hom is triangulated. Its value on a finite free cell vanishes by the completed-coefficient free-resolution theorem and the same criterion. A splitting maps to a splitting, so the value on a finite-free retract is zero. The kernel is a triangulated subcategory: shifts preserve zero and the middle object of a distinguished triangle with zero endpoints is zero. Apply bounded homotopy-category devissage to this kernel and then transport through quotientCompQhIso and the restriction comparison. Reverse the local criterion. Rank zero and inverted support intervals are allowed.

theorem boundedProjectiveComplex_complete
    (P : CochainComplex (scalarReductionSource l E T) ℤ)
    (hb : ∃ a b : ℤ, ∀ k : ℤ, k < a ∨ b < k → IsZero (P.X k))
    (hP : ∀ k : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      ∃ i : P.X k ⟶ ∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
        (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E T)),
      ∃ p : (∏ᶜ (fun _ : Fin r ↦ SheafOfModules.unit
        (completedIntegralCoefficientSheafUnrestricted l E T))) ⟶ P.X k,
      i ≫ p = 𝟙 _) :
    IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete l E T none (DerivedCategory.Q.obj P)
